result:
mitmweb now uses `_mitmproxy_xsrf` as its XSRF cookie instead of `_xsrf`, so a stale HttpOnly `_xsrf` cookie no longer affects it. I haven't run any tests or built the frontend.

- **Backend:** `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` now sets `xsrf_cookie_name="_mitmproxy_xsrf"` in the `Application` settings, next to `xsrf_cookies=True`.
- **Frontend:** `web/src/js/utils.ts` now reads `_mitmproxy_xsrf` in `fetchApi` when it sets the `X-XSRFToken` header.

I didn't touch any tests. I searched `web/src` and `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` for other `_xsrf` references and found none. I didn't search the Python `test/` directory, so a test that hardcodes `_xsrf` could still exist there.
